title: Ultrasound-Guided Fascia Hydrorelease for Groin and Hip-Related Pain: A Multi-Point Clinical Protocol
content: Background and Objectives: Chronic groin and hip-related pain encompasses four clinical presentations—groin pain, anterior thigh pain, hip-related low back pain, and lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (LFCN) pain—together with two working definitions used in our practice: frozen hip and hip-related ischaemic pain. This clinical protocol, based on our clinical experience, organises the hip-region fascia intervention points as a multi-point system with a stepwise bedside evaluation and describes ultrasound-guided fascia hydrorelease (FHR) in a reproducible form. Materials and Methods: Narrative synthesis of targeted literature searches and more than a decade of our clinical observation; no formal consensus process or new prospective dataset. The points were classified into seven anatomical groups and described with in-house ultrasound images and supplementary videos. Results: Nineteen intervention points are presented: adductor-related (3); iliopsoas-related (3); pubic-related (1); hip joint-related (7, including the anterior capsule and the three capsular ligaments addressed by passive release); inguinal ligament-related (1); others (3); perivascular (1). Conclusions: The bedside correspondences and ultrasound criteria are based largely on our clinical experience and have not been validated. FHR is proposed not as a stand-alone treatment but as one element of multimodal care in which the period of pain relief is used to resume active exercise; prospective validation is required.
